gap: No result ChatGPT got states Jackery's own limits for its top 'best for carrying' pick, the Explorer 1000 v2: each DC8020 solar port is capped at 200 W and both together at 400 W (16–60 V); three panels are not supported; mixed panel wattages are not supported; four panels need two SolarSaga adapters; car input is limited to 8 A; and solar and car charging cannot run at the same time.
standout_why: Compared against backup-power.org (cited, 2026-11-04) and thepowerstationguide.com (cited, 2026-02-01). enoughwatts.com and unpluggedwatts.com failed to load with a TLS certificate error, so they were not compared. backup-power.org lists Jackery solar only as '400 W', with no per-port cap and no connector or panel-count rules, and it calls the Jackery's 12 V/10 A car port, which is an output. thepowerstationguide.com says it 'could not confirm solar input or expansion specs for the v2'. Both rivals already say the C1000 Gen 2 and Explorer 1000 v2 do not expand and the DELTA 3 Plus reaches 5 kWh, so the expansion story is not new. thepowerstationguide's claims that the DELTA 3 expands to 5 kWh and the AC180 takes B80/B230/B300 batteries could not be checked against a maker page. backup-power.org says the AC180 is 'fixed'.
decides: This confirms the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 for carrying, since Jackery lists it at about 10.8 kg (about 23.8 lb), but adds a caveat for solar campers. Its 400 W solar ceiling, split as 200 W per port, is lower than the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (600 W) and BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,000 W), and it cannot use a three-panel setup. A shopper who wants fast solar recharging or one extra battery later should look at the Elite 100 V2, which is 1.5 lb heavier, or the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus instead. The DELTA 3 Plus is the only expandable 1 kWh model among these.

findings.label: Solar input connector and limits
findings.value: 2 × DC8020 in parallel, 16–60 V; one port 10.5 A / 200 W max; both ports 21 A / 400 W max
findings.note: Maker FAQ. A single panel cannot exceed 200 W of input, whatever the panel's rating.

findings.label: Solar panel configuration rules (maker exclusions)
findings.value: 1, 2 or 4 panels supported; 3 panels not supported; panels of different wattages not supported at the same time; 4 panels need 2 × SolarSaga adapters; each port needs the same panel model and count
findings.note: Charge times Jackery lists: SolarSaga 100 ×2 about 8 h, ×4 about 4 h; SolarSaga 200 ×2 about 3.8 h. SolarSaga 40/80 are listed as 'No Verified Data'. SolarSaga 500 X is listed as '/', meaning no data.

findings.label: Car charging input
findings.value: 12–16 V, 8 A limit whether one or both DC inputs are used; about 12 h from a car socket; about 3 h with Jackery's car fast charger
findings.note: 12–16 V × 8 A = 96–128 W. Jackery says solar plus car charging at once, and two car cables at once, are both 'Not supported'.

findings.label: Expansion battery / parallel / UPS
findings.value: Battery packs: not supported; parallel operation: not supported; UPS switchover is not 0 ms, and Jackery says not to use it for servers or workstations
findings.note: Same FAQ lists 32.7 × 22.4 × 24.7 cm and about 10.8 kg.

findings.label: Solar input and expansion
